## What I fixed, and why


## What I fixed, and why

### Fix 1 — Contact page navigation
Commit: 596f63a

During manual testing, I noticed that the Contact page did not have navigation links to the main application.

I added links to Tasks, New task and Contact in templates/contact.html. I tested the navigation in Chrome and confirmed that it works.

### Fix 2 — Flask Debug Mode
Commit: 059e9ff

During the code review, I identified that Flask Debug Mode was enabled.

I changed debug=True to debug=False in app.py to reduce the risk of exposing debugging information. I restarted the application and confirmed that the terminal displayed "Debug mode: off".

Both issues were identified through manual verification rather than Gemini's original findings.

## What I am knowingly leaving, and why

The application does not currently include CSRF protection. It has no authentication and is being developed locally for the course. The security implications need to be reviewed before the application is made publicly accessible.

## What the reviewer got wrong

Gemini incorrectly reported that the contact route was missing. I had already tested this route successfully.

Gemini also referred to a file called task_list.html, which does not exist in the project. The "Hello from Leandro" message is in index.html and was intentionally preserved from my Week 1 coursework.

This review showed me that AI-generated findings must be checked against the actual code and application behaviour.

## Second Review — app.py

I asked Gemini to review app.py separately because the first review focused mainly on HTML templates.

Gemini identified missing CSRF protection in the POST forms. This is a real security concern that needs further evaluation.

However, Gemini incorrectly reported that the contact templates were missing. I confirmed that both files exist and tested the contact form successfully.

Gemini also suggested SQLite WAL mode and custom error pages. These are possible future improvements, but they are not required for the current application.

This second review showed me that AI can report problems that do not exist, even after receiving the application code.
